sections.what_happened: [ATTRIBUTED REPORT] Tehran has received US Vice President JD Vance's letter to SNSC secretary Mohsen Rezaei but has not yet responded, Tasnim reported ('Iran has received the letter but has not yet responded'); Fars carried a similar account citing a source familiar with the matter. Reuters adds its own reporting effort: Iran's UN mission and Vance's office did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Tasnim adds Tehran insists on its seven conditions and 'any position that undermines this firm framework is unacceptable'. This FLIPS totw-20261029-2000-01 from HOLD to PASS: the 2000 scan's stated flip condition (a second declared-tier family) is met twice over.
sections.what_verified: Reuters (T1) and AFP (T1) independently published the Tasnim/Fars receipt reporting in-window, each with its own byline/reporting. Origin chain Tasnim/Fars remains Iranian state-affiliated and undeclared, so the UNDERLYING receipt still rests on Iranian media; what is now strongly supported is the attributed-report fact. NYT 'received well / response expected Thursday' line still reaches this scan only via carries (ZeroHedge, suaragarut - both undeclared), NOT counted.
sections.what_disputed: Trump's on-record framing conflicts with the letter-as-peace-channel reading: contact concerned medical supplies, not peace talks he directed ('No' when asked if he directed Vance to restart talks). No Iranian official statement quoted directly; no US confirmation of receipt in-window. Fars source dismisses international-media speculation about the letter's contents as not reflecting the truth.
sections.why_matters: Tehran got the letter, hasn't answered: wire confirmation lands the receipt story, the clock to November 3 is the story
sections.context: Background: UPDATE + GATE FLIP to totw-20261029-2000-01 (HOLD) -- Vance-letter receipt now wire-corroborated in-window: Reuters + AFP pickups (Khaleej Times 20:05 ; JPost/Reuters update 20:11 )

Is the Vance letter a genuine off-ramp before the post-midterm strike window, or a cover story while strikes are prepared?
